analysis: The reference image shows a baby stroller whose expected motions are the four wheels rotating continuously about their horizontal axles and a sunshade canopy folding back along a transverse revolute joint. With six parts across the frames, I allocate a point budget roughly as: sunshade ≈ 2.5, wheels collectively ≈ 1.5 (≈ 0.4 each). The four wheels are cleanly segmented and stay visually unchanged across every frame — correct physics for geometrically symmetric parts rotating around their symmetry axes, no deduction. The sunshade rotates back away from the seat in a plausible folding direction, but as the motion progresses the canopy panel visibly clips into the seat-back and frame tubes of the stroller, which indicates the revolute axis is offset from the true hinge line (likely sitting slightly forward of the seat back rather than exactly on the pivot edge). The direction and range of the sunshade motion are correct but the position of its axis is imperfect, costing roughly one point off the 4-point budget. All other parts are static as expected — score 4.
